story.originalTitle: Villeneuve: Verstappen showed 'race craft' edge over Mercedes pair in Vegas
story.summaryEn: Former Formula 1 world champion Jacques Villeneuve says Max Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix victory shows that Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will not be able to beat the Red Bull driver next year unless they have a superior car.
detailZh: 雅克·维伦纽夫表示，马克斯·维斯塔潘在拉斯维加斯大奖赛中展现出了对乔治·拉塞尔和基米·安东内利的“驾驶技术”优势。
马克斯·维斯塔潘顶住了梅赛德斯车手乔治·拉塞尔和基米·安东内利的压力，为红牛赢得了一场激动人心的拉斯维加斯大奖赛；本周末卡塔尔大奖赛将在天空体育直播，排位赛于周六18点进行，正赛于周日16点进行。
乔治·拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯大奖赛尝试超越队友基米·安东内利时锁死轮胎撞上护栏，这让对手马克斯·维斯塔潘十分高兴。
前F1世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫表示，马克斯·维斯塔潘在拉斯维加斯大奖赛的胜利表明，除非拥有更优赛车，否则梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔明年无法击败这位红牛车手。
维斯塔潘从杆位起步后守住了领先位置，但在几乎整场50圈的比赛中先后受到拉塞尔和安东内利的挑战，全场位置几乎不断变化，不过这位红牛车手巧妙地化解了他们最好的攻势，随后两人都在后期出现失误，排名下滑。
安东内利已在梅赛德斯赛季初的统治性表现帮助下建立起显著优势，从而加冕2026年世界冠军，但维斯塔潘正以令人不安的状态为这一年收官，这位四届世界冠军赢下了最近六场比赛中的四场，并连续九次登上领奖台。

2026年拉斯维加斯大奖赛精彩集锦
天空体育F1评论员、1997年F1世界冠军维伦纽夫在赛后表示：“这很精彩。人们会说所有超车都有电池的参与，但这并不重要。
“我们看到了些赛车技巧。马克斯更胜一筹，而两位梅赛德斯车手在这方面有所欠缺。
“这告诉我们的是，除非明年梅赛德斯拥有一辆更优越的赛车，否则他们无法获胜，因为有些东西缺失了。”
乔治·拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯大奖赛起步时与马克斯·维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔缠斗。
多种因素共同作用，其中最突出的是尾流效应的极强威力，使得在拉斯维加斯大道赛道上进行的这场令人窒息的比赛中出现了超过350次超车。
领先位置易手34次，但每次维斯塔潘被超越——几乎每次都是被梅赛德斯车手超越——这位四届世界冠军都会在几个弯道内夺回位置。
拉塞尔在比赛尾声试图超越安东内利争夺第二名时锁死轮胎并撞上护栏，随后这位意大利车手在最后一圈开始时因准备向维斯塔潘发起最后挑战时错误地松开油门而遭遇动力损失。
马克斯·维斯塔潘在赢得拉斯维加斯大奖赛后，对长期对手乔治·拉塞尔说了几句简短的话。
维伦纽夫也对七届世界冠军刘易斯·汉密尔顿和去年的总冠军得主兰多·诺里斯的驾驶表现印象深刻，后者利用梅赛德斯车队的失误获得第二名，领先于他的迈凯伦队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里。
如果不是在与法拉利队友夏尔·勒克莱尔的一次有争议的碰撞中打转，汉密尔顿本也可能登上领奖台。
“你可以看到刘易斯和兰多一样，都有很好的比赛技巧，”维伦纽夫补充道。

“看到这一幕真的很有趣。我们今天看到的是一场不需要进站、不需要轮胎衰退的比赛。
“我们有一场车手可以一直像排位赛圈那样全力推进的比赛，这让他们能够真正地竞速。非常有趣。”

detailEn: Max Verstappen showed 'race craft' edge over George Russell and Kimi Antonelli during Las Vegas GP, says Jacques Villeneuve

Max Verstappen withstood pressure from Mercedes' George Russell and Kimi Antonelli on his way to winning a thrilling Las Vegas GP for Red Bull; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
George Russell hits the barrier after a lock-up when trying to overtake team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, much to the delight of rival Max Verstappen

Former Formula 1 world champion Jacques Villeneuve says Max Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix victory showed that Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will not be able to beat the Red Bull driver in next year's championship unless they have a superior car.

Verstappen retained the lead from pole position at the start but was challenged by Russell and then later Antonelli for almost the entire 50-lap race amid near constant changes of position throughout the field, but the Red Bull driver expertly saw off their best efforts before both made late errors to drop down the order.

Antonelli has already been crowned 2026 world champion after Mercedes' dominance early in the season helped him build a significant advantage, but Verstappen is putting together an ominous finish to the year, with the four-time world champion having won four of the last six races and claimed nine successive podiums.

Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix
Sky Sports F1 pundit and 1997 F1 world champion Villeneuve said after the race: "It was exciting. People will say there was a battery involved [in all the passes], but it doesn't matter.
"We saw some race craft. Max was above and the two Mercedes drivers were lacking in that respect.
"And what it is telling us is that unless next year Mercedes have a car that's superior, they can't win because there's something missing."
George Russell tussles with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadajr at the start of the Las Vegas Grand Prix
A combination of factors, most notably the extreme power of the slipstream effect, meant there were more than 350 overtakes during a breathless race at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit.
The lead changed hands 34 times, but every time Verstappen was overtaken, which on almost every occasion was by a Mercedes, the four-time world champion retook his position within a few corners.

Russell locked up and hit a barrier as he tried to pass Antonelli for second in the closing stages, before the Italian suffered a loss of power at the start of the final lap after incorrectly lifting off the throttle as he was preparing to mount a final challenge to Verstappen.
Max Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe George Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Villeneuve was also impressed by the drives of seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and last year's title winner Lando Norris, who took advantage of the Mercedes errors to finish second ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton could have also ended up on the podium had it not been for him spinning in a contentious collision with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc.
"You could see that Lewis had good race craft as well as Lando," Villeneuve added.
Watch new angles of the collision between Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas Grand Prix
"It was really fun to see. We saw today a race where you don't need pit stops, you don't need tyres that degrade.
"We had a race where drivers could push like qualifying laps all the time and that allowed them to race. It was great fun."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
